title: Getting back into RPG Maker after 16 years

posts.author: Tarrund
posts.body:
Hey yall.
I used to play around with RPG Maker VX and visit the forums way back in 2009 (some ogs I remember if they're still around: Touchfuzzy, Scherzo, Lieutenant Zaidi, Mr. M, Paulcellx ). Finally dipping back into RPG making and it's great to see this rad little community alive and well.
A little about me: I enjoy video games (RPGs, couch coop, indies, some shooters), the outdoors, making zines, and comics.
A lot has probably changed since I last tinkered with this stuff—any tips on good MV/MZ resources, what to look into, or where to start again would be hugely appreciated. Thanks!

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Probably the same thing we tell every new guy. Do the built in tutorials, learn how the engine works. Figure out what game you wanna make and what system it's gonna have, then browse for resources to accomplish that.
Plugin and asset "shopping" as I call it rarely leads to a good and well thought out game. At the very least it's prone to feature creep because there's all this "cool stuff your game definitely needs now".
Either way, welcome back to our little cult. Good luck with your project!

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome back! You will probably see a huge difference in the newer engines (MV or MZ).
Depending on how much experience you have, I usually recommend finding a YouTube tutorial series that goes from the basics to more advanced concepts and then recreate those. That is how I started learning, but I also had no experience with RPG Maker or any sort of programming.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!

posts.author: Myahalna
posts.body: Welcome back! I just got back into rpg maker also and can say quite a bit has changed from what I used to MZ. The tile size and language change was the biggest surprise to me
